disclaimer: Reference ranges provided are for educational and dietary context only. They do not constitute a medical diagnosis. Please consult a qualified physician or healthcare provider for interpretation.

ranges.label: Low (Hypoglycemia range)
ranges.explanation: Values below 70 mg/dL are lower than the standard fasting reference range.

ranges.label: Normal Fasting Glucose
ranges.explanation: Normal fasting blood glucose is typically between 70 and 99 mg/dL.

ranges.label: Impaired Fasting Glucose
ranges.explanation: Fasting blood glucose between 100 and 125 mg/dL indicates elevated fasting glucose.

ranges.label: Elevated Fasting Glucose
ranges.explanation: Fasting glucose of 126 mg/dL or higher exceeds normal fasting thresholds.

fasting_blood_glucose.source: American Diabetes Association (ADA) Standards of Medical Care

ranges.label: Normal Glycated Haemoglobin
ranges.explanation: HbA1c below 5.7% is within normal reference limits for average 3-month blood glucose.

ranges.label: Borderline / Prediabetes range
ranges.explanation: HbA1c between 5.7% and 6.4% indicates elevated average blood sugar over the last 90 days.

ranges.label: Elevated Glycated Haemoglobin
ranges.explanation: HbA1c of 6.5% or higher reflects persistently elevated blood glucose levels.

ranges.label: Optimal
ranges.explanation: LDL cholesterol below 100 mg/dL is generally considered optimal.

ranges.label: Borderline High
ranges.explanation: LDL cholesterol between 100 and 159 mg/dL is above optimal levels.

ranges.label: High
ranges.explanation: LDL cholesterol of 160 mg/dL or greater is elevated.

ldl_cholesterol.source: National Cholesterol Education Program (NCEP) ATP III

ranges.label: Low HDL (Major risk factor)
ranges.explanation: HDL cholesterol below 40 mg/dL is considered low protective cholesterol.

ranges.label: Acceptable
ranges.explanation: HDL cholesterol between 40 and 59 mg/dL is in the standard acceptable range.

ranges.label: Optimal (Cardioprotective)
ranges.explanation: HDL cholesterol of 60 mg/dL or higher is considered protective.

ranges.label: Normal
ranges.explanation: Fasting triglycerides below 150 mg/dL are normal.

ranges.label: Borderline High
ranges.explanation: Triglycerides between 150 and 199 mg/dL are borderline elevated.

ranges.label: High
ranges.explanation: Triglycerides of 200 mg/dL or greater are high.

ranges.label: Low
ranges.explanation: Haemoglobin below 12.0 g/dL is below standard adult reference levels.

ranges.label: Normal
ranges.explanation: Standard adult reference interval is 12.0 to 17.5 g/dL.

ranges.label: Elevated
ranges.explanation: Haemoglobin above 17.5 g/dL is above typical reference ranges.

ranges.label: Deficient
ranges.explanation: 25-hydroxyvitamin D below 20 ng/mL is considered deficient.

ranges.label: Insufficient
ranges.explanation: Vitamin D between 20 and 29 ng/mL indicates insufficient levels.

ranges.label: Sufficient
ranges.explanation: Vitamin D between 30 and 100 ng/mL is generally considered sufficient.

ranges.label: Elevated / Potential Toxicity
ranges.explanation: Vitamin D above 100 ng/mL exceeds optimal levels.

ranges.label: Low / Deficient
ranges.explanation: Vitamin B12 below 200 pg/mL is classified as deficient.

ranges.label: Borderline
ranges.explanation: Vitamin B12 between 200 and 300 pg/mL is borderline low.

ranges.label: Normal
ranges.explanation: Standard normal reference range is 300 to 900 pg/mL.

ranges.label: Elevated
ranges.explanation: Vitamin B12 above 900 pg/mL exceeds normal physiological levels.

vitamin_b12.source: National Institutes of Health (NIH) Office of Dietary Supplements
